edition.intro: This week's edit is all about making what you already own work harder, from clever winter layers to jeans, boots and pants that earn their place.

items.title: How to Layer Clothes for Winter Without Looking Like Joey From Friends: A Step-by-Step Guide
items.snippet: A step-by-step layering guide with tips from our favorite street style stars
items.headline: How to Layer for Winter Without Looking Like Joey From Friends
items.summary: Glamour's guide treats layering as a bit of trial and error, built on contrasting or matching colors and a mix of sheer and solid fabrics. Staggering your hemlines, letting a little hosiery peek out and adding belts, scarves or chunky leg warmers keep the look balanced instead of bulky.
items.tip: Put on three layers and check that each one ends at a different point on your body before you leave the house.

items.title: Black Skinny Jeans Are Chic Again—Especially With These Shoes
items.snippet: And they look surprisingly good with all the winter trends.
items.headline: Black Skinny Jeans Are Back, and the Shoes Make the Outfit
items.summary: After a long run of baggy denim, slim black jeans are working again because they are so easy to dress up or down. The magic is in the footwear, with pointed flats, low heels, ankle boots, soft loafers and tall boots all giving a different mood. A clean, snug fit with no bunching at the ankle lets the shoe take center stage.
items.tip: Try your black jeans with a pair of pointed flats and fold the hem once to show a bit of ankle.

items.title: 20 Years On, Kate Moss’s Winter Boots, Jeans and Knit Combo Is Still Influencing Chic Londoners
items.headline: Kate Moss's 2003 Jeans, Knit and Boots Formula Still Works
items.summary: A skinny jean, slouchy navy knit and brown knee-high boots combo from two decades ago is being worn again on London streets. The outfit works because every piece is a simple staple and the cuffed boots add a distinctive finish. High street boots in brown suede or leather make it easy to recreate on a modest budget.
items.tip: Pair slim jeans with a relaxed navy sweater and brown tall boots, and fold the top of the boots over for the cuffed look.

items.title: These Casual It Pants Keep Selling Out—Here's How I'm Dressing Them Up For Fall and Winter
items.snippet: Seven outfits that show their versatility.
items.headline: Dressing Up Casual Pull-On Pants for Fall and Winter
items.summary: One fashion editor shows that relaxed poplin pants, usually seen as a summer item, can work all through the colder months. She styles them with faux fur, a barn jacket, brocade, leather and a sweatshirt, then adds polish with flats, pumps or scarves. The lesson is that the outer layer and shoes do the dressing up.
items.tip: Take a casual pair of pants you wear in summer and style them with a textured jacket and a smart shoe.

items.title: Buying Your First Pair of Selvedge Jeans? Start Here
items.snippet: A highly subjective guide to 10 of the most-discussed selvedge denim silhouettes of all time.
items.headline: Buying Your First Pair of Selvedge Jeans
items.summary: Raw selvedge denim is having a revival, and the choice of brands and cuts can feel overwhelming. GQ's writer narrows it down to a list of long-loved Japanese, Canadian and American makers, noting fit, weight and leg shape for each. Straight and relaxed-straight cuts in mid-weight denim are a friendly place to start.
items.tip: Before buying any new jeans, note the weight and leg shape of the pair you wear most and shop for something similar.

items.title: On the Hunt for Hair-Matching Earmuffs à la Hunter Schafer
items.snippet: “Blade Runner: 2099” star Hunter Schafer donned a pair of sci-fi heroine-coded earmuffs—some winter headgear you can expect to see everywhere.
items.headline: Hair-Matching Earmuffs Are Having a Moment
items.summary: Hunter Schafer wore fuzzy earmuffs that matched her hair as part of a press tour look inspired by a 2007 Undercover collection. Other stars have embraced fluffy earmuffs too, and the trend fits a wider interest in playful headwear. You can find vintage pairs on resale sites or new ones from a range of brands.
items.tip: Pick up a pair of fuzzy earmuffs in a shade close to your hair and wear them with a simple coat.

items.title: 44 Best Wedding Guest Dresses in 2026 for Every Type of Ceremony
items.snippet: Shop the best wedding guest dresses for every kind of ceremony and dress code—from a garden wedding to a beach wedding and courthouse ceremony.
items.headline: How to Choose a Wedding Guest Dress for Any Season or Dress Code
items.summary: Vogue's roundup sorts wedding guest dresses by season, dress code and setting, showing there is room for personality within each. The basic rules are to read the invitation carefully, let the season guide your color and avoid white or anything that looks bridal. Texture, silhouette and accessories can make a simple dress feel special.
items.tip: Reread the invitation and check the dress code before you choose, then pick a color that suits the season.

practice: Putting it into practice: Start by shopping your closet. Pull out your black jeans, a slouchy sweater, any pair of brown or black boots, a lace or sheer skirt and a scarf or belt. Try the jeans three ways with pointed flats, loafers and boots, and test layering the skirt over trousers or a long-sleeve tee under a short-sleeve one, staggering the hems so each layer ends in a different spot.

If you do buy something, keep it small and versatile: a pair of brown knee-high boots from the high street, or a pair of pointed flats if you do not own a good pair. Fuzzy earmuffs are a cheap way to add personality. Use your best staples like relaxed pants and one good dress as a base, then add a textured jacket, a scarf or a bit of hosiery, so every purchase works with several outfits you already have.
